criteriaSource: CLAUDE.md C4 severity definitions (High / Medium / QA-Low)

codeVerified.BatchNFTMinter.sol:230-266: Read at HEAD. Gate at line 246 is purely count-based (_nudgeSize != 0 && count >= _nudgeSize); payout at 251-253 transfers the FULL balanceOf(this) of the nudge token to a caller-chosen recipient with no comparison against value paid. Up-front equality guard at 230-233 is unconditional on nudgeSize.
codeVerified.yield-claim-nft/src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol: registerDispatcher (125) takes initialPrice with no >0 check; setPrice (282) takes newPrice with no >0 check; mint (159/164) does safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, dispatcher, price) — at price==0 this is a permissionless, zero-cost mint. price==0 is a structurally-supported state. Confirms DEDUP-001 sub-vector (a) precondition is real.

classification.assetImpact: The entire externally-funded nudgePaymentToken pot is transferred to a caller-chosen recipient. Repeatable as the pot refills. Direct loss of protocol/sponsor assets.
attackPath: 1. Protocol funds the nudge pot (any amount); pinned dispatcher config.price == 0 (NFTMinterV2 permits this; no price>0 validation anywhere).
2. Attacker calls batchMint with count >= nudgeSize, recipient = attacker. Each nftMinter.mint transfers price (0) — mints are free.
3. count >= nudgeSize clears the count-only gate at line 246.
4. Full nudge-token balance (the whole pot) is transferred to the attacker at lines 251-253 for ~zero token cost (gas only).
5. Repeat whenever the pot is refilled.
Sub-vector (b) — over-funded pot at non-zero price:
1. Independent owner knobs leave pot > nudgeSize * price (no on-chain coupling forces pot <= cost).
2. Attacker calls batchMint with count == nudgeSize, paying nudgeSize*price.
3. Gate clears; attacker receives the full pot > amount paid. Net profit = pot - nudgeSize*price.
classification.likelihood: high - sub-vector (a) needs only a funded pot while the pinned dispatcher sits at price==0 (a normal-operations configuration NFTMinterV2 explicitly supports, not an attacker-supplied input or admin blunder); sub-vector (b) needs only pot > nudgeSize*price, which two independent owner knobs make reachable with no on-chain guard against it. Both are permissionless once the precondition holds.
classification.assumptions: Pot is funded (the feature's purpose). For (a): pinned dispatcher price==0. For (b): pot exceeds total mint cost for nudgeSize mints.
classification.externalRequirements: A cross-contract config state in the sibling NFTMinterV2 (price==0 for sub-vector (a)). This is a protocol-supported, non-exotic operating state, not an attacker-controlled input — it does not weaken the path to a hypothetical.

classifiedFindings.justification: Meets High: assets (the full nudge pot) are directly drained to an attacker via a concrete, permissionless, executable path with no hand-wavy hypotheticals. The only precondition is a supported configuration (price==0 pin, or pot > cost), confirmed reachable by reading NFTMinterV2 (no price>0 validation on registerDispatcher/setPrice and free mints at price==0). story-014 fixed only the caller's CHOICE of minter/token; the value-blind gate — the literal root cause that the in-code NatSpec records as having previously drained mainnet — survives unchanged. I considered downgrading to Medium because sub-vector (a) leans on an operational config rather than a pure attacker input, but C4 High explicitly allows indirect paths with a valid attack route, and (b) is permissionlessly profitable with no misconfig at all (only pot>cost, which nothing on-chain prevents); the impact is full, direct, repeatable asset theft. This is a partial-fix REGRESSION of prior H-01 and inherits at least its High severity; flagged prominently. Plausible (not Implausible) High: no validator collusion or black-swan economics required.
classifiedFindings.humanReviewFlag: Live exploitability of sub-vector (a) at a specific block depends on the deployed pinned dispatcher's price. If price==0 on the relevant pinned dispatcher, this is squarely a regression of H-01 via the surviving root cause; finding-manager should set regressionOf=H-01.

classification.assetImpact: The nudge pot is paid to a front-running searcher instead of the honest qualifying minter. No protocol-owned asset is created or destroyed beyond the pot, but value is leaked away from the honest caller, who still pays mint cost + gas and receives zero nudge.
attackPath: 1. Honest user broadcasts a qualifying batchMint (count >= nudgeSize) with recipient = self.
2. A searcher observes the mempool, copies the call with recipient = searcher and a higher priority fee.
3. Searcher's tx lands first; the winner-take-all full-balance payout transfers the whole pot to the searcher.
4. The honest user's tx executes against an empty pot (nudgeAmount == 0): they pay mint cost + gas, mint the NFTs, and receive no nudge.
classification.likelihood: medium - fully permissionless and config-independent on any public mempool, but the searcher must itself pay nudgeSize mint cost + a competitive priority fee, so it is only net-positive when the pot exceeds that outlay (i.e. it collapses into / overlaps DEDUP-001 sub-vector (b)'s over-funded condition for profitability). The honest caller is harmed (loses the expected nudge and their gas) regardless of searcher profitability.
classification.assumptions: Public mempool; a pot worth racing for; an honest caller who expects the nudge.
classification.externalRequirements: Mempool visibility / a competitive block-builder market. No owner misconfiguration required.

classifiedFindings.justification: Meets Medium, not High: this is a value leak from an honest caller via a mempool race with stated assumptions (public mempool, fundable pot) and an external requirement (block-builder/priority-fee market). No protocol-owned asset is stolen in a way the protocol did not intend to give away — the pot was always destined to a qualifying minter; the defect is that the WRONG party (a parasitic front-runner) captures it and an honest participant is denied the incentive, degrading the function/fairness of the nudge mechanism. It does not reach High because the searcher's gain is bounded by and conditioned on the pot exceeding their own mint+gas outlay (an external/economic requirement), and there is no direct drain of protocol principal independent of an honest caller's own transaction. Distinct root cause from DEDUP-001 (mechanism/mempool race vs. value-blind gate) and a distinct mitigation surface (commit-reveal / sender-bound recipient / per-spend accounting), so kept separate.

classification.assetImpact: None on current code. ERC1155 onERC1155Received fires on the caller-chosen recipient mid-loop while max approval is live and paymentAmount is held, but the full-balance payout is idempotent to zero, the held paymentAmount is the attacker's own budget, the approval is bounded to the contract's own balance, and NFTStaker uses independent OZ-guarded storage. Sanitizer adjudicated NOT-EXPLOITABLE for third-party fund loss.
attackPath: 1. Reentrancy is reachable (recipient callback mid-loop) but no state read after the callback can be manipulated to extract extra funds on current code.
Defensive gap only; becomes High only under speculative future changes (fixed-amount payout or retained per-caller balance).
classification.likelihood: n/a - no demonstrated fund-loss path on current code; severity rests on defense-in-depth and parity with the sibling NFTStaker, which does inherit ReentrancyGuard.
classification.assumptions: Standard ERC token; current payout semantics unchanged.
classification.externalRequirements: None for the gap; a future code change for any real impact.

classifiedFindings.justification: QA/Low: a missing-guard defensive gap with no demonstrated asset impact on current code. Per CLAUDE.md, speculation on future code without a demonstrated current root cause does not justify HM; classifying higher would overstate. Maps to prior L-01; carry forward in the QA bundle, recommend adding nonReentrant for parity with NFTStaker.

classification.assetImpact: None. Uncapped caller-supplied count loop; a large count exceeds the block gas limit and reverts the caller's own transaction. Per-iteration mint cost is the intended economic friction for the nudge gate.
attackPath: 1. Caller passes an oversized count; their own tx runs out of gas and reverts. No third party is affected; no funds at risk.

classifiedFindings.justification: QA/Low: caller self-DoS / gas-griefing with no impact on other users, protocol availability, or funds. State/usability robustness nit. Maps to prior L-02; carry forward in QA bundle.

classification.assetImpact: None. The up-front equality guard (lines 230-233) reverts whenever nudgePaymentToken == paymentToken, unconditionally on nudgeSize, before the nudgeSize gate at 245-246. So a configured-but-equal nudge token bricks every batchMint even when nudge is disabled via nudgeSize==0 and no payout would ever occur.
attackPath: 1. Owner config has nudgePaymentToken == paymentToken with nudgeSize == 0 (nudge disabled).
2. Every batchMint reverts despite no payout being possible — an overbroad guard / spec-vs-behavior mismatch.
classification.likelihood: n/a - configuration usability issue, no attacker, no fund loss.
classification.assumptions: Owner sets nudge token == payment token while nudge is size-disabled.

classifiedFindings.justification: QA/Low: a spec-deviation / usability nit (an overbroad revert in a harmless configuration), no asset risk and no availability impact in any intended operating mode. Confirmed unchanged at HEAD. Maps to prior L-03; carry forward in QA bundle.

regressions: DEDUP-001 (regression of prior H-01 via surviving value-blind root cause)
